8 recommended medical diet clinics in Shibuya! Compare prices, drugs, features, etc. of each plan

 

“I want to undergo a medical diet in Shibuya, which clinics do you recommend?”

As mentioned above, many people may feel that there is too much information and it is difficult to make a decision.

There are several clinics in the Shibuya area that support medical diets.Drugs handled, fee structure, and treatment stylevaries greatly depending on the clinic.

Annotation

*1: Applicable conditions are listed on the application page.
Split fees using a credit company designated by the clinic

*2: General price is the price that does not apply monitor discounts such as photo disclosure.
(Cannot be used in conjunction with other bonus campaigns)
[Monitor recruitment requirements]
For both men and women: Those who can cooperate with weight measurement before and after the start of treatment and questionnaires regarding treatment.
(Other details will be provided at the time of counseling)
This is the price when the campaign is applied.
Not covered by insurance as it is a free medical treatment.
Posted prices are subject to change without notice.

In this article:Recommended clinics that handle medical diets in ShibuyaWe will introduce 8 hospitals.

In addition,Characteristics and differences of major drugs, estimated monthly costs, and how to deal with side effectsI will also explain.

We organize the information based on three points: type of drug, budget, and visiting style, so please use this as a reference when choosing the clinic that suits you.

What you can learn from this article
  • Characteristics and differences of GLP-1 injection, Manjaro, Libersus, Ugobi, and Canaglu
  • Three criteria for choosing the right drug for you: injection or oral administration
  • 5 criteria for choosing a medical diet clinic in Shibuya

Types and characteristics of main drugs used in medical diets

Medications prescribed for medical diets are divided into several types depending on their mechanism of action and administration method.

GLP-1 receptor agonistDepending on whether you choose injections or oral medications, the style of hospital visits and estimated costs will change.

Summary of characteristics of the 5 main drugs handled in Shibuya
  • GLP-1 receptor agonist: Injectable drug that suppresses appetite and stabilizes blood sugar
  • Manjaro: High weight loss effect due to dual action of GLP-1 and GIP
  • Libersus: Oral GLP-1 drug that does not require injections
  • Ugobi: Once-a-week injection drug that has been approved in Japan and is covered by insurance.
  • Canaglu: Oral SGLT2 inhibitor that excretes sugar in the urine

The main drugs treated at clinics in the Shibuya area are:GLP-1 injection, Manjaro, Libersus, Ugobi, CanagluThere are 5 types.

Each drug has a different mechanism of weight loss and dosage frequency, soChoose a drug that suits your lifestyle and constitutionThis will lead to continued treatment.

GLP-1 receptor agonist is an injection drug that suppresses appetite and stabilizes blood sugar levels.

GLP-1 receptor agonists are hormones secreted after meals.GLP-1It is a drug that simultaneously suppresses appetite and stabilizes blood sugar levels by strengthening the action of .

It has the effect of slowing down the rate at which stomach contents are sent to the intestines, so even small meals canEasily feel fullIt will be.

Typical products prescribed in medical diets include once-weeklyOzempicor require daily administration.victozaand so on.

Main characteristics of GLP-1 receptor agonists
  • Strengthens the function of the postprandial hormone GLP-1 and simultaneously promotes appetite suppression and blood sugar stability
  • Slows gastric emptying, making it easier to feel full even with small meals
  • Representative product: once a weekOzempic, administered daily.victoza
  • Administration method: Subcutaneous injection into the abdomen/thigh (technical instructions provided at the clinic)
  • Initial side effects (nausea, diarrhea) often subside within 2 to 4 weeks.

The basic method of administration is subcutaneous injection, which is often self-injected into the abdomen or thigh, and is generally administered at home after receiving instructions on how to do it at a clinic.

Regarding the weight loss effect, clinical data shows thatLoss of appetite within a few weeks of starting treatmentMany people have reported seeing this.

The use of GLP-1 receptor agonists may be contraindicated in patients with a history of pancreatitis or thyroid-related diseases. Please be sure to declare this in advance during your medical interview.

Nausea and diarrhea tend to occur as initial side effects, but in many cases, from the start of administration2-4 weeksIt calms me down.

Manjaro can be expected to improve weight loss due to the dual action of GLP-1 and GIP.

Manjaro acts on both GLP-1 and GIP receptorsdual agonistreported approaches to weight loss compared to single GLP-1 drugs.

GIPis a hormone that promotes insulin secretion, and works synergistically with GLP-1 to suppress appetite and burn fat.

In overseas clinical trials,72 weeksApproximately of body weight with administration of20% reductionThere is a group that has achieved this, and results have been confirmed that are superior to GLP-1 alone.

Basic data of Manjaro
  • Mechanism of action: Dual agonist of GLP-1 receptor + GIP receptor
  • Frequency of administration: once weekly subcutaneous injection
  • Starting dose: Increase gradually from 2.5mg
  • Clinical efficacy: Some groups achieved approximately 20% weight loss in 72 weeks
  • Shibuya area market price: Upper 20,000 yen to 40,000 yen per month (free medical treatment)

It can be administered by subcutaneous injection once a week, and the dose is2.5mgThe design is to start with and gradually increase the amount.

At clinics in the Shibuya area, prescriptions are commonly offered at free clinics, and the monthly fee varies depending on the dose of the drug.Market price ranges from high 20,000 yen to 40,000 yen.It is.

Manjaro is a strong option for people who have not had sufficient results with GLP-1 drugs or who are looking to lose weight in a shorter period of time.

However, in Japan, approval procedures are underway as of 2024 as an obesity treatment drug, so please check in advance which clinics can prescribe the drug before visiting.

Libersus is an oral GLP-1 drug for people who don't like injections.

Libersus is a component of a GLP-1 receptor agonistSemaglutideIt is an oral medication in the form of tablets, and is an option prescribed to people who want to avoid injections.

Water once a day immediately after waking upWithin 120mLand after taking it.30 minutesshould avoid eating, drinking, and taking other medications.

Libersus dosage rules and cost guidelines
  • Dosage timing: Immediately after waking up, take within 120mL of water
  • Avoid eating, drinking, and other medicines for 30 minutes after taking the medication.
  • Dose: Increase gradually from 3mg → 7mg → 14mg
  • Shibuya area monthly cost: Approximately 15,000 yen for 7mg, approximately 20,000 yen for 14mg
  • The effects are slightly slower than injections, but they do not require injections and are easy to continue.

If you do not follow the rules regarding dosing timing, the absorption rate of the drug will be significantly reduced. Please strictly follow the instructions given.

The weight loss effect is the same as the injectable drug Ozempic, but due to the absorption rate during oral administration, the same dose may not be effective.The effect is slightly slower than injectable drugs.There is a tendency.

The tablet is3mg・7mg・14mgThere are three types, and the standard prescription is to start with 3mg and increase the dose gradually.

The monthly cost in the Shibuya area varies depending on the dose, but for 7mgAround 15,000 yen, at 14mgAround 20,000 yenis the standard.

This drug is easy to use for those who want to reduce the hassle of going to the hospital or those who prefer online medical treatment, so please consult with your doctor to see if it suits your lifestyle.

Ugobi is a once-weekly injection approved in Japan as a treatment for obesity.

Ugobi is a GLP-1 receptor agonist whose active ingredient is semaglutide.2023This is an injectable drug that has been officially approved in Japan as a treatment for obesity.

Since it has been approved in Japan, it is recommended for patients who meet the conditions of BMI and comorbidities.Can be prescribed through insurance medical treatmentThis makes it very different from other drugs.

The conditions for insurance coverage are:BMI 35 or more, or have a BMI of 27 or higher and have hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia.merge two or moreIf you are.

Ugobi insurance coverage conditions
  • Obese patients with a BMI of 35 or more
  • BMI 27 or higher and 2 or more of hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia
  • If the above conditions are met, the co-payment of drug costs will be reduced to 30%.
  • For free medical treatment: The average monthly fee is between 30,000 yen and 50,000 yen.

By subcutaneous injection once a week,0.25mgstarting from up to2.4mgThe design is such that the amount can be increased in stages.

The monthly fee for receiving prescriptions at free medical treatment is30,000 yen to 50,000 yenThere are many cases where the out-of-pocket costs are higher than those covered by insurance.

If you meet the insurance coverage conditions, you can significantly reduce costs by choosing a clinic that prescribes Ugobi as part of your insurance treatment.

Before your visit, please check your BMI and presence of complications, and inquire with the clinic to see if your insurance will cover it.

Oral medications such as Canaglu, which are repurposed diabetes medications, are also options.

Kanaguru isSGLT2 inhibitorIt is an oral drug that is classified as a drug and was originally developed as a treatment for type 2 diabetes, but its weight loss effect has been recognized and it has been used as a medical diet.

SGLT2 inhibitors inhibit sugar reabsorption in the kidneys,Excretes excess sugar from the body as urineThis is how you burn calories.

What is SGLT2 inhibitor?

An oral drug that suppresses sugar reabsorption in the kidneys and burns calories by excreting excess sugar in the urine. Although it does not have the appetite suppressing effect of GLP-1 drugs, the simple administration method of just one tablet per day makes it easy to continue. Another feature is that it is easy to keep costs down, ranging from 5,000 yen to 10,000 yen per month.

Although it does not have the appetite suppressing effect of GLP-1 drugs,1 tablet per dayThe simple administration method, which requires only one dose, is easy to continue.

Monthly costs are lower compared to GLP-1 drugs;From 5,000 yen to 10,000 yenMany clinics prescribe it, so it is suitable for those who want to keep costs down.

SGLT2 inhibitors may increase the risk of urinary tract infections and genital infections. If you feel any discomfort while taking this medicine, please consult your doctor immediately.

In addition to Kanaguru,FarxigaYaJardianceThere are clinics that handle the same type of drugs, so please consider the prescription lineup when choosing a clinic.

Decision-making guideline for choosing the drug that suits you: injection or oral administration

Medications prescribed for medical diets areAdministration method・Basically, choose based on three points: weight loss effect and frequency of hospital visits.

Oral medications are available for those who are not comfortable with injections, while injectable medications are suitable for those who prioritize higher efficacy.

Three criteria for selecting drugs
  • If you are not comfortable with injections: Oral medications such as Libersus and Canaglu are candidates.
  • If you are looking for a high weight loss effect: GLP-1 injection Manjaro is suitable
  • Frequency of hospital visits/possibility of self-injection: Choose the administration method that suits your lifestyle

The monthly cost varies depending on the type of drug, soCompare your lifestyle and budgetHowever, please consult your doctor.

If you are not comfortable with injections, oral medications such as Libersus may be an option.

If you are resistant to injections, take an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist.Libersusis the main candidate.

Libersus is a drug that is taken once a day, 30 minutes before meals, and only requires a visit to the clinic for the prescription.

Since there is no need to administer the injection at home, it is suitable for people who are concerned about handling syringes or who want to avoid administering it at work or outside.

Estimated monthly cost isLate 10,000 yen to around 30,000 yenCompared to injectable drugs, it is relatively low cost and easy to start using.

However, oral medicationsManagement of dietary restrictions and medication timingSince it is directly linked to the effect, it is necessary to work on it in parallel with reviewing your lifestyle habits.

There is a rule to take Libersus with less than 120mL of water on an empty stomach, otherwise the active ingredients will be difficult to absorb. Please ask your doctor for details on how to take the medicine when prescribing the medicine.

Kanaguruis an oral drug that is classified as an SGLT2 inhibitor, and uses a different mechanism than GLP-1 drugs to lower blood sugar levels and reduce weight.

There are multiple options for oral medications, so check with your doctor about the side effects and differences in medication styles before making your choice.

If you are looking for higher weight loss effects, GLP-1 injections are suitable.

If a high weight loss effect is a priority, use GLP-1 injections or GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists.Manjarois an option.

Clinical trial data shows that Manjaro is a once-weekly subcutaneous injection.Average weight loss of 15-20%have been reported, and can be expected to be more effective than oral medications.

Approximate weight loss effects and costs of injection drugs
  • Manjaro: Average weight loss of 15-20% reported in clinical trials
  • Ugobi: Applicable for obesity, and can be covered by insurance if the BMI and comorbid conditions are met.
  • Monthly cost: around 30,000 to 60,000 yen (budget design based on long-term continuation is required)
  • Self-injectable drugs can be administered at home after learning the procedure at the clinic.

Ugobi is also an injection that is administered once a week, and is approved for obesity, and is prescribed when the conditions for BMI and comorbidities are met.

Manjaro and Ugobi are designed to be administered starting from a small amount and gradually increasing the dosage to maximize effectiveness while minimizing side effects.

On the other hand, for injection drugs, the monthlyAround 30,000 yen to 60,000 yenThis tends to increase costs, so it is necessary to design a budget that assumes long-term continuation.

In the case of drugs that can be self-injected, once you learn the procedure at a clinic, you can administer them at home, reducing the number of hospital visits.

Please choose a drug that suits your target weight and treatment period by considering the balance between high efficacy, cost, and administration method.

Frequency of hospital visits and whether self-injection is possible also influence drug selection.

Depending on the type of medication, the timing and frequency of clinic visits will vary.

Oral medications such as Libersus and Canaglu require regular hospital visits for each prescription.Clinics that support online medical treatmentIf so, you can continue your prescription without having to visit the hospital.

Injectable drugs are divided into two types: those that are injected at a clinic and those that are self-injected at home.

The clinic injection type requires a visit every time, so if you are visiting the Shibuya area, access from your workplace or home will have a direct impact on whether or not you can continue visiting the clinic.

Comparison of characteristics by hospital visit style
  • Oral medication (Libersus Canaglu): Only hospital visits for each prescription. Clinics that support online treatment do not require a visit to the hospital.
  • clinic injection type:Requires hospital visit every time. Access from Shibuya Station is the key to continuity
  • self-injectable: Can be administered at home after initial procedure instruction. Comply with syringe management and disposal rules

Self-injectors can be administered at home after receiving initial instruction, but it is necessary to properly manage and dispose of the syringe.

Continuing to administer the drug without proper self-injection techniques may lead to skin induration and the risk of infection. Be sure to receive guidance at the clinic before starting.

If you have difficulty commuting to the hospital, you can create an environment that makes it easier for you to continue receiving treatment by choosing a clinic that supports online consultations and mail-order prescriptions.

The effect of the drug isproportional to durationTherefore, check in advance whether the hospital visit style and drug administration method suit your lifestyle.

5 criteria for choosing a medical diet clinic in Shibuya

There are several medical diet clinics in the Shibuya area.Drug lineup, cost structure, treatment stylevaries greatly depending on the clinic.

Don't make a decision based only on the first free consultation,Is it possible to continue going in the long term?Comparing clinics based on five criteria will help you choose a clinic with no regrets.

Five points of comparison when choosing a clinic
  • ① Drug lineup: Check if the drug you want is available
  • ② Monthly total: Compare actual costs including initial consultation fee, test fee, and drug fee.
  • ③ Medical treatment format: Does the hospital support both online medical treatment and in-office treatment?
  • ④Doctor's medical department: Determine whether a consultation system for side effects is in place.
  • ⑤Access/Clinical hours: Check the route from Shibuya Station and availability at night and on weekends.

After sorting out the following five factors: drug type, monthly cost, treatment format, doctor's response system, and access, choose a clinic that matches your priorities.

Check whether the lineup of drugs we handle matches your wishes.

The types of drugs that clinics can prescribe vary by medical institution.

GLP-1 injectionThere are clinics that deal with all drugs such as Ozempic, Victoza, Manjaro, Libersus, Ugobi, and Canaglu, while others only deal with oral medications such as Libersus.

Injectable and oral drugsWeight loss effect and monthly costPlease check the clinic's website or contact us in advance to see if they carry the drug you want.

Points to check drug lineup
  • Check the prescription examples of the desired drug (Manjaro, Ugobi, etc.) in advance on the web or by phone.
  • Clinics that handle both injectable and oral medications have a wide range of options for changing medications.
  • Check whether you can switch to another drug if the effect is insufficient or the side effects are strong.

Relatively new drugs such as Manjaro and Ugobi are not available at all clinics. If you have decided on the drug you want, please check to see if there is a prescription for it before making your reservation.

Another factor to consider when choosing a clinic is whether or not they can accommodate you if you want to switch to a different drug midway through the treatment.

If the clinic handles multiple drugs, it may be difficult to obtain an effect or the side effects may be strong.Drug change optionsIt becomes easier to hold.

Compare costs based on monthly total including initial consultation fee, re-examination fee, and drug fee

When comparing medical diet costs, consider not only drug costs.Total monthly fee including initial examination fee, re-examination fee, and blood test feeLet's decide.

While some clinics make drug costs look low, there are cases where they adopt a fee structure in which initial consultation fees and management fees are charged separately.

Quick reference table for monthly expenses
  • Libersus (oral): around 10,000 to 20,000 yen per month (over 30,000 yen for initial consultation fee and test fee in the first month)
  • GLP-1 injection drugs (Ugobi, Ozempic, etc.): Approximately 25,000 to 40,000 yen per month
  • Manjaro: Around 30,000 to 50,000 yen per month
  • Estimated duration: 3 to 6 months. Some plans cost more than 150,000 to 300,000 yen in total.

LibersusIn this case, the average monthly cost is around 10,000 to 20,000 yen, but if you include the initial consultation fee and blood test, the first month will be around 10,000 to 20,000 yen.Over 30,000 yenThere are many cases where this happens.

Top GLP-1 injection drugs such as Manjaro and Ugobi cost a monthly feeApproximately 25,000 yen to 40,000 yenis the general market price.

If a clinic says things like "first month free" or "monitor price", be sure to check the regular fees from the second month onward. If you don't compare the total ongoing costs, you run the risk of giving up on going to the hospital midway through.
